Here's What to Do Now
 Kailey Hagen, CFP®, The Motley Fool Thu, October 22, 2026 at 7:20 AM CDT 3 min read The Social Security Administration has announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for 2027. This is above average compared with the last 50 years of COLAs, and it's expected to add roughly $75 per month to the typical retirement benefit. 
 That will give the average senior about $900 more per year, but it might be less than what you were hoping for. It's possible you will get a larger benefit boost if your current checks are above average. But if not, you may have to resort to the following moves listed below to pay for what Social Security won't provide next year. 
 Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » 
 Image source: Getty Images. Rely more heavily on personal savings 
 The most straightforward option if you have substantial personal savings is to withdraw more from your retirement accounts to supplement your Social Security benefits. Add 3.6% to your current Social Security checks to get a rough idea of how much more you'll get from the program next year. Then, subtract this amount from your average monthly expenses to see how much you'll need from your personal savings. 
 If you're concerned about running out of savings prematurely, review your budget to identify areas where you could cut back on spending. When this isn't feasible, you may have to try the other strategies listed here. 
 Consider a part-time job 
 Working in retirement may not be how you'd envisioned this chapter of your life, but it can give you a steady source of income to supplement your personal savings and your Social Security benefits. Some people also enjoy the sense of purpose and the chance to socialize that a job gives them. 
 You don't have to work in the same career you spent your life in. You're free to choose something more in line with your interests or with a flexible schedule that fits your lifestyle. Even if it only covers half your monthly expenses, that could help you stretch your personal savings over several more years. 
 Apply for other government benefits 
 If working isn't an option for you and your personal savings aren't enough to cover your costs, you may need to look into other government benefits to cover your expenses in 2027. There are programs that can help you pay for essentials like housing, groceries, utilities, and healthcare, so you can reserve your savings for expenses that fall outside of these categories. 
 Story Continues Applying and getting approved for these benefits can take time, so it's best to start the process now if you expect to need them next year. Reach out to your state social services agency to learn what types of benefits might be available to you. 
 The $23,760 Social Security bonus most retirees completely overlook 
 If you're like most Americans, you're a few years (or more) behind on your retirement savings. But a handful of little-known "Social Security secrets" could help ensure a boost in your retirement income. For example: one easy trick could pay you as much as $23,760 more ... each year! Once you learn how to maximize your Social Security benefits, we think you could retire confidently with the peace of mind we're all after.
